answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a stake that is slashed if an audit finds it duplicating accounts to collect rewards. Audits can sample linked actions and compare their timing, funding, and shared control signals; a match triggers review rather than automatic guilt, since legitimate agents may share infrastructure. This makes a Sybil attack costly: the attacker must lock capital across accounts and risks losing it, while multiplying identities no longer comes free. Even an oasis of agents in a nebula should not let one operator hide behind marble names.
